reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because the calls were recorded to help viewers recognize fraudulent caller behavior and were presented as a warning. The narrator identifies the interaction as fake and says Apple would not direct viewers to those websites, while the records do not show that the requested connection was completed or that any loss occurred.

citations.quote: I have been receiving multiple calls from scammers and several today so I recorded a few in case you speak to someone so you know what they might tell you.
If you get a call, just hang up.
So, there is an example of a fake scam call.
It seems to receive automatic calls from Apple server, regarding your iCloud account.
Within 24 hours we have received notification that your account has been locked in overseas multiple times.

opening.argument: The interaction links a promised account-security outcome to a concrete viewer action: the caller says a senior technician will run a security scan, then instructs the listener to enter an external address so the caller can connect to supposed support. That is a solicitation pathway, even though the promised benefit is technical assistance rather than cash or an asset. The combination of an alleged compromised account, a requested browser action, and remote connection creates the kind of low-friction external flow that can acquire access or control. The evidence does not establish that the connection was completed, but it does show the action-and-promised-outcome pairing.

citations.quote: a senior technician will run a security scan on your device
you need to type that address so that I can connect to the Apollo support
on the top of the address bar you need to write www.helpme.net

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the recording a warning describes the narrator's later framing, but it does not remove the solicitation captured in the call. The caller still pairs an alleged account problem with instructions to visit an external site and connect to support. The fact that the narrator tells viewers to hang up does not establish that the requested flow was harmless; it shows the narrator recognized the interaction as something viewers should avoid.

citations.quote: If you get a call, just hang up.
a senior technician will run a security scan on your device
on the top of the address bar you need to write www.helpme.net

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The action-and-outcome pairing is evidence of what the caller solicited, not proof that the video itself offered an asset or that anyone surrendered access. The recording shows only instructions to type an address and a claimed scan; it does not show completion, payment, data transfer, or loss. The narrator explicitly characterizes the exchange as an example of a fake call, which is consistent with documenting the solicitation rather than promoting it.

citations.quote: So, there is an example of a fake scam call.
Okay sir, open Google Chrome.
Oh, they hung up.

opening.argument: Several concrete red flags appear together: the caller invokes an Apple server, claims the account was locked from overseas locations, creates a time-sensitive security concern, and directs the listener to an outside website for a supposed scan. The caller also presents a junior-to-senior technician handoff, which can make the requested connection appear more authoritative. These signals support treating the interaction as deceptive solicitation. Although no monetary reward is mentioned, this is the closest available category because a simple external verification or support flow is linked to a promised account-security resolution.

citations.quote: It seems to receive automatic calls from Apple server, regarding your iCloud account.
Within 24 hours we have received notification that your account has been locked in overseas multiple times.
a senior technician will run a security scan on your device
right now there are some suspicious activities that was detected in your devices

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the narrator's warning as dispositive, but the caller's own conduct remains the central evidence: an alleged account compromise is used to drive the listener toward an external site and supposed Apple connection. Saying that no loss is shown addresses the result, not the deceptive pressure and external-flow signals that precede it. The caller's claimed Apple identity and security emergency are not neutral background details.

citations.quote: you need to type that address so that I can connect to the Apollo support
they're calling from a caller ID showing as if it's an Apple Store so just be warned it's not an Apple Store calling
Within 24 hours we have received notification that your account has been locked in overseas multiple times.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Those signals are precisely why the material is a warning: it exposes the caller's claims so viewers can recognize them. The recording does not authenticate the claims, show a completed connection, or establish that the video asks viewers to follow them. Instead, the narrator says the call is fake and warns that Apple will not make this request, so the red flags support an anti-scam investigation rather than a scam offer.

citations.quote: So, there is an example of a fake scam call.
Apple is not going to call you and get you to go to those sites.
I have been receiving multiple calls from scammers and several today so I recorded a few in case you speak to someone so you know what they might tell you.

opening.argument: The footage can be read as more than commentary because it preserves and demonstrates a direct support-style solicitation: the caller asks the listener to open a browser, enter a named destination, and connect to an alleged Apple server for technical help. That sequence is operational and participation-oriented, regardless of the narrator's surrounding commentary. The external destination and promised assistance give viewers a concrete pathway to act, while the asserted Apple connection supplies credibility. The available evidence does not prove a completed scam, but it does show the promotional mechanics of steering someone into the flow.

citations.quote: Once you are in front of the computer just let me know.
you need to type that address so that I can connect to the Apollo support
you will be connecting to apple online support

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense labels the surrounding content a warning, but the captured call still performs the persuasive work of steering a person to a destination under an Apple-support pretext. A warning label does not change what the caller asks the listener to do. Nor does the absence of a completed connection eliminate the solicitation; the relevant pathway is plainly presented before the caller hangs up.

citations.quote: you will be connecting to apple online support
on the top of the address bar you need to write www.helpme.net
Oh, they hung up.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The alleged promotional mechanics belong to the caller being investigated, not to the video's editorial purpose. The narrator identifies the call as fake, tells viewers to avoid it, and describes the Apple-store presentation as bogus. The material therefore exposes the pathway so viewers can reject it; it does not promise viewers support, direct them to participate, or show that the destination was used successfully.
